name: rea
description: Reverse engineer anything with agents, from app behavior down to native binaries.
one_liner: Hands an AI assistant the tools to figure out how any app or program works internally, down to the raw machine code, instead of a human doing that detective work by hand.
buyer: A security consultant or legacy-software contractor who bills clients to figure out how an undocumented app, driver, or old binary works before they can fix, clone, or audit it.
business_use_cases: A security firm uses it to speed up malware triage and vulnerability research, cutting billable hours per engagement.
A contractor hired to keep a 15-year-old program alive with no source code uses it to reconstruct how key features work before touching anything.
A compatibility-layer vendor uses it to understand undocumented native libraries they need to re-implement for a new platform.

money_ideas.idea: Offer a 'legacy app autopsy' reverse-engineering service for old or undocumented software, priced per engagement.
Sell prebuilt analysis playbooks for specific binary formats or platforms to security teams.

steal_this: A paid service: point this at a client's old undocumented .exe or firmware dump over a weekend and hand back a plain-English report of what it actually does.
